Where it began

Shamar Joseph was born on 31 August 1999 in Baracara, a small community far up the Canje River in eastern Guyana, two days by boat from New Amsterdam. Phones and the internet barely reached it. He learned the game in the village, copying the West Indies greats Curtly Ambrose and Courtney Walsh, and since proper balls were scarce he bowled with tape balls, lemons, limes, guavas and even balls of melted plastic.

Work came first. He felled timber in the logging trade, then moved to New Amsterdam, where he was a building labourer and later a security guard on 12-hour shifts. In time he gave up the job to try cricket full time.

The player

His break came through Romario Shepherd, who introduced him to the Guyana set-up. He took 6 for 13 on his debut in Division 1 cricket, went to a fast-bowling clinic run by Ambrose himself, and made his first-class debut for Guyana in February 2023. By the end of that year he had helped Guyana Amazon Warriors win the Caribbean Premier League and toured South Africa with West Indies A.

His Test debut came at Adelaide in January 2024. With his very first ball he had Steve Smith caught, and he took five wickets in that first innings. Eleven days later, in the second Test, he took 7 for 68 in under 12 overs and West Indies won by eight runs. It was 27 years since they had last won a Test in Australia. He was player of the series in his first series, the first West Indian to manage that.

By November 2026 he had played 17 Tests from 2024 to 2026, with 69 wickets at 24.94 and four five-wicket innings.

What made him special

He was a right-arm fast bowler from the start, and even in his first CPL games he could bang in short balls at more than 140 kph, over after over. Above all he has a gift for big moments: a wicket with his first ball, five on debut, and the last wicket of a Test that West Indies fans will not quickly forget.

He could bat a bit, too. Coming in at number 11 on debut, he made 36, the best by a West Indian number 11 in a first Test.

Away from the middle

He became the first cricketer from Baracara to play Tests, and in January 2024 the first West Indies player to be named the ICC's Men's Player of the Month. His success took him to franchise cricket too, with Lucknow Super Giants in the IPL and Peshawar Zalmi in the Pakistan Super League.

And finally

He grew up bowling guavas at village batsmen. Steve Smith, the first man he dismissed in Test cricket, may be relieved he got a proper ball.
